With a length of {{convert|213|km|mi|abbr=on}}, it is Japan's ninth longest river.

Its source is {{ill|Lake Suwa|en|Lake Suwa|qid=Q1206692|lt=Lake Suwa}} in the [[Kiso Mountains]] near {{ill|Okaya, Nagano|en|Okaya, Nagano|qid=Q838672|lt=Okaya}} in {{ill|Nagano Prefecture|ace|Prefektur Nagano|af|Nagano-prefektuur|an|Prefectura de Nagano|ar|ناغانو (محافظة)|arz|محافظه ناجانو|az|Naqano prefekturası|azb|ناقانو اوستانی|ban|Préféktur Nagano|be|Нагана (прэфектура)|bg|Нагано|bn|নাগানো প্রশাসনিক অঞ্চল|ca|Prefectura de Nagano|cdo|Nagano-gâing|ce|Нагано (префектура)|ceb|Nagano-ken|ckb|پارێزگای ناگانۆ|cs|Prefektura Nagano|cy|Nagano (talaith)|da|Nagano-præfekturet|de|Präfektur Nagano|eo|Gubernio Nagano|es|Prefectura de Nagano|et|Nagano prefektuur|eu|Nagano (prefektura)|fa|استان ناگانو|fi|Naganon prefektuuri|fr|Préfecture de Nagano|frr|Nagano (Prefektüür)|ga|Maoracht Nagano|gl|Prefectura de Nagano|hak|Nagano-yen|he|נאגנו (מחוז)|hr|Nagano (prefektura)|hu|Nagano prefektúra|hy|Նագանո (պրեֆեկտուրա)|id|Prefektur Nagano|ilo|Prepektura ti Nagano|it|Prefettura di Nagano|ja|長野県|ka|ნაგანოს პრეფექტურა|kaa|Nagano prefekturası|kn|ನಾಗನೊ (ಪ್ರಾಂತ್ಯ)|ko|나가노현|la|Naganoënsis|lt|Nagano prefektūra|lv|Nagano prefektūra|mk|Нагано (префектура)|mni|ꯅꯥꯒꯥꯅꯣ ꯂꯝꯈꯥꯢ|mr|नागानो प्रांत|ms|Wilayah Nagano|ne|नगानो|nl|Nagano (prefectuur)|no|Nagano (prefektur)|nov|Nagano Prefekture|os|Нагано (префектурæ)|pam|Prepektura ning Nagano|pl|Prefektura Nagano|pnb|ضلع ناگانو|pt|Nagano|ro|Prefectura Nagano|ru|Нагано (префектура)|sco|Nagano Prefectur|se|Nagano prefektuvra|sh|Prefektura Nagano|si|නගානො ප්‍රාන්තය|simple|Nagano Prefecture|sk|Nagano (prefektúra)|sl|Prefektura Nagano|sr|Префектура Нагано|su|Nagano Prefecture|sv|Nagano prefektur|sw|Mkoa wa Nagano|tg|Префектураи Нагано|th|จังหวัดนางาโนะ|tl|Prepektura ng Nagano|tr|Nagano (prefektörlük)|tt|Нагано (префектура)|uk|Нагано (префектура)|ur|ناگانو پریفیکچر|vi|Nagano|war|Nagano (prefektura)|wuu|长野县|zh|长野县|zh_classical|長野縣|zh_min_nan|Nagano-koān|zh_yue|長野縣|qid=Q127877|lt=Nagano Prefecture}}. It then flows through {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|en|Aichi Prefecture|qid=Q80434|lt=Aichi Prefecture}} and western {{ill|Shizuoka Prefecture|en|Shizuoka Prefecture|qid=Q131320|lt=Shizuoka Prefecture}}.

[[File:Tenryu river - from sky - sept 30 2016.jpg|thumb|From the air, 2016]]

==Geography==
The Tenryū River is the only river exiting Lake Suwa. It follows a generally southern course. The upper reaches of the river in the Ina Basin of Nagano Prefecture are a rich agricultural area. The river exits through a gap between the [[Kiso Mountains]] (Central Alps) and the {{ill|Akaishi Mountains|en|Akaishi Mountains|qid=Q415350|lt=Akaishi Mountains}} (Southern Alps), which forms the border between Shizuoka and Nagano Prefectures . This area is characterized by heavy rainfall (up to 3,000&nbsp;mm per year) and deep V-shaped valleys. Continuing south through Shizuoka Prefecture, the river drains a wide coastal plain noted for fruit and rice production. The city of [[:en:Hamamatsu, Shizuoka|Hamamatsu]] is near the {{ill|River mouth|en|River mouth|qid=Q1233637|lt=River mouth}} at the {{ill|Philippine Sea|en|Philippine Sea|qid=Q159183|lt=Philippine Sea}}.

==History==
The Tenryū River is mentioned in {{ill|Nara period|en|Nara period|qid=Q189178|lt=Nara period}} records as the {{nihongo|Violent Tenryū |暴れ天竜|Abare-Tenryū}} for its fast, turbulent flow and its propensity to flood. The upper portion of the river (in {{ill|Shinano Province|en|Shinano Province|qid=Q289250|lt=Shinano Province}}) was referred to as the Tenryūgawa, whereas the lower portion (in {{ill|Tōtōmi Province|en|Tōtōmi Province|qid=Q1048864|lt=Tōtōmi Province}}) was often referred to as the {{nihongo|Aratama River|麁玉川|Aratama-gawa}}. In various entries in the national historical chronicle ''[[Shoku Nihongi]]'', flooding of the river is mentioned in the years 710 CE and 765 CE. Records through the {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|qid=Q193292|lt=Heian period}} and {{ill|Kamakura period|en|Kamakura period|qid=Q236205|lt=Kamakura period}} are sparse, but from the {{ill|Muromachi period|en|Muromachi period|qid=Q334845|lt=Muromachi period}}, increasing efforts at [[:en:Flood control|Flood control]] were made by various warlords and landholders along the river by construction of dikes, {{ill|Levee|en|Levee|qid=Q105190|lt=Levee}}s, and channels.

With the occupation of {{ill|Hamamatsu Castle|en|Hamamatsu Castle|qid=Q1152352|lt=Hamamatsu Castle}} by {{ill|Tokugawa Ieyasu|en|Tokugawa Ieyasu|qid=Q171977|lt=Tokugawa Ieyasu}}, considerable efforts were made to increase the revenues of Tōtōmi Province through creation of new rice fields with irrigation from the Tenryū River. However, flooding remained a problem, including a great flood in 1674 which washed away many of the earthen works of previous centuries.

===Transport===
During the {{ill|Edo period|en|Edo period|qid=Q184963|lt=Edo period}}, the {{ill|Tōkaidō (road)|ckb|ڕێگای تۆکایدۆ|cs|Tókaidó|da|Tōkaidō|de|Tōkaidō|el|Τοκάιντο (δρόμος)|es|Carretera Tōkaidō|et|Tōkaidō|eu|Tōkaidō (errepidea)|fa|توکایدو (جاده)|fi|Tōkaidō|fr|Tōkaidō|id|Tōkaidō (jalan)|it|Tōkaidō (strada)|ko|도카이도 (도로)|nl|Tokaido (weg)|pl|Tōkaidō (droga)|pt|Tōkaidō (estrada)|ro|Tōkaidō|ru|Токайдо (дорога)|simple|Tōkaidō (road)|sl|Tokaido (pot)|sv|Tōkaidō|tr|Tōkaidō (yol)|uk|Східноморський шлях|zh|东海道 (路名)|qid=Q963514|lt=Tōkaidō}} (road) developed as the major highway linking {{ill|Edo|ar|إيدو|arz|ايدو (تجمع سكان فى توشيما ديستريكت)|be|Эда (горад)|bn|এদো|br|Edo (kêr)|bs|Edo|ca|Edo (Japó)|ckb|ئێدۆ|cs|Edo|cy|Edo|da|Edo (Japan)|de|Edo|el|Έντο|eo|Edo|es|Edo|et|Edo|eu|Edo (Tokio)|fa|ادو|fi|Edo|fr|Edo (ville)|hr|Edo (Tokio)|hu|Edo|id|Edo (Jepang)|it|Edo (città)|ja|江戸|ka|ედო|ko|에도|lt|Edas|ml|ഏഡോ|mn|Эдо|mr|एडो|ms|Edo|nl|Edo (Japan)|no|Edo (by)|pl|Edo (miasto)|pt|Edo|ru|Эдо (город)|simple|Edo|sl|Edo (mesto)|sq|Edo|sv|Edo|th|เอโดะ|tr|Edo|uk|Едо (місто)|ur|ادو|vi|Edo|wuu|江戶|zh|江戶|zh_classical|江戶|zh_yue|江戶|qid=Q215646|lt=Edo}} with {{ill|Kyoto|en|Kyoto|qid=Q34600|lt=Kyoto}}, and ''[[:en:Daimyō|Daimyō]]s'' from the western {{ill|Han system|ca|Han (Japó)|cs|Han (Japonsko)|de|Han (Japan)|es|Han (Japón)|fa|هان (ژاپن)|fi|Daimiokunta|fr|Han (Japon)|he|האן (יחידה אדמיניסטרטיבית)|hu|Hanrendszer|id|Sistem han|it|Han (Giappone)|ja|藩|ko|번 (행정 구역)|mk|Хан (Јапонија)|ms|Sistem han|nl|Han (grondgebied)|pl|Han (Japonia)|pt|Han (território)|ru|Хан (владение)|sl|Han sistem|tr|Han (Japonya)|uk|Хан (Японія)|vi|Hệ thống các phiên|zh|藩 (日本)|qid=Q841985|lt=domains}} were forced to travel on a regular basis to Edo to attend to the ''{{ill|Shogun|en|Shogun|qid=Q131767|lt=Shogun}}'' in a system known as ''[[sankin-kōtai]]''. However, the [[Tokugawa shogunate]] prohibited the building of bridges over major rivers as a security measure. As depicted in contemporary ''[[ukiyo-e]]'' prints by artists such as {{ill|Hokusai|en|Hokusai|qid=Q5586|lt=Hokusai}}, travelers crossed the river on  [[:en:ferryboat|ferryboat]]s, as the current was too fast and too deep for fording. In cases of bad weather or high waters, they were forced to stay several days (or even several weeks) beside the river at [[shukuba|post stations (''shukuba'')]] such as {{ill|Mitsuke-juku|fr|Mitsuke-juku|ja|見附宿|ko|미쓰케슈쿠|pl|Mitsuke-juku|qid=Q782144|lt=Mitsuke-juku}}.

The river was bridged shortly after the [[Meiji Restoration]] by road and railroad bridges. Today the [[:en:Tōkaidō Shinkansen|Tōkaidō Shinkansen]] {{ill|Express train|ar|قطار إكسبريس|bn|এক্সপ্রেস ট্রেন|ca|Tren exprés|cs|Rychlík (vlak)|de|Schnellzug|el|Τρένο εξπρές|es|Tren semidirecto|eu|Tren laster|fr|Train express|he|רכבת אקספרס|hi|एक्सप्रेस ट्रेन|hu|Gyorsvonat|id|Kereta api ekspres|it|Treno espresso|ja|急行列車|ko|급행열차|lmo|Treno espress|ml|എക്സ്പ്രസ് തീവണ്ടി|nl|Sneltrein|no|Ekspresstog|pl|Pociąg pospieszny|pt|Trem expresso|ro|Tren expres|ru|Скорый поезд|simple|Schnellzug|sk|Rýchlik (vlak)|sq|Ekspresi|sr|Ekspresni voz|sv|Snabbtåg|ta|விரைவுத் தொடருந்து|uk|Швидкий поїзд|zh|急行列車|qid=Q964162|lt=express train}} crosses the river in a few seconds.

==Hydroelectric development==
The potential of the Tenryū River valley for hydroelectric power development was realized by the {{ill|Government of Meiji Japan|ar|حكومة ميجي في اليابان|es|Gobierno Meiji|fa|دولت میجی|fr|Gouvernement de Meiji|id|Pemerintahan Meiji Jepang|ms|Kerajaan Meiji Jepun|no|Meijiregjeringen|pt|Governo Meiji|th|รัฐบาลเมจิ|vi|Chính quyền Minh Trị|qid=Q1322181|lt=Government of Meiji Japan}} at the start of the 20th century. The Tenryū River was characterized by a high volume of flow and a fast current. Its mountainous upper reaches and tributaries were areas of steep valleys and abundant rainfall, and were sparsely populated. However, the bulk of investment in hydroelectric power generation in the region was centered on the {{ill|Ōi River|ar|نهر أوي|ceb|Ōi Gawa (suba sa Hapon, Shizuoka-ken)|de|Ōi (Fluss)|fa|رود اوی|fr|Ōi-gawa|ja|大井川|ko|오이강|my|အိုးအိမြစ်|ru|Ои (река)|wuu|大井川|zh|大井川|qid=Q1044017|lt=Ōi River}}, and it was not until the {{ill|Taishō era|en|Taishō era|qid=Q329174|lt=Taishō era}} that development began on the Tenryū River.

Private entrepreneur [[Fukuzawa Momosuke]] founded the {{nihongo|Tenryūgawa Electric Power|天竜川電力|Tenryūgawa Denroku}}, which later became {{nihongo|Yahagi Hydroelectric|矢作水力|Yahagi Suiroku}} before it was nationalized into the pre-war government monopoly {{nihongo| Japan Electric Generation and Transmission Company|日本発送電株式会社| Nippon Hassoden K.K.}} in 1938. The first dam on the main stream of the Tenryu River, the {{ill|Yasuoka Dam|arz|سد ياسوكا|ceb|Yasuoka-damu|ja|泰阜ダム|uz|Yasuoka to‘g‘oni|qid=Q8050080|lt=Yasuoka Dam}} was completed in 1935. This was followed by the {{ill|Iwakura Dam|ja|岩倉ダム|uz|Iwakura to‘g‘oni|qid=Q6100426|lt=Iwakura Dam}} in 1938. The {{ill|Hiraoka Dam|arz|سد هيراوكا|ceb|Hiraoka-damu|fr|Barrage d'Hiraoka|ja|平岡ダム|uz|Hiraoka to‘g‘oni|qid=Q5769450|lt=Hiraoka Dam}} was started in 1938, but completed until 1951 due to the start of {{ill|Pacific War|ar|حرب المحيط الهادئ|az|İkinci Dünya müharibəsində Sakit okean cəbhəsi|azb|ایکینجی دونیا ساواشیندا بؤیوک اوقیانوس جبهه‌سی|ba|Икенсе донъя һуғышының Тымыҡ океан хәрби хәрәкәттәр театры|ban|Yuda Pasifik|be|Ціхаакіянскі тэатр ваенных дзеянняў Другой сусветнай вайны|bg|Тихоокеански театър (Втора световна война)|bn|প্রশান্ত মহাসাগরীয় যুদ্ধ|br|Brezel ar Meurvor Habask (1937-1945)|bs|Rat na Pacifiku|ca|Guerra del Pacífic|ckb|شەڕی پاسفیک|cs|Druhá světová válka v Tichomoří|da|Stillehavskrigen|de|Pazifikkrieg|el|Πόλεμος του Ειρηνικού|eo|Pacifika Fronto|es|Guerra del Pacífico (1937-1945)|et|Sõda Vaiksel ookeanil|eu|Pazifikoko gerra|fa|جنگ اقیانوس آرام|fi|Tyynenmeren sota toisessa maailmansodassa|fr|Guerre du Pacifique|gn|Paraguasu Py'aguapy Ñorairõ (1937-1945)|ha|Yakin Pacific|he|המערכה באסיה ובאוקיינוס השקט|hi|प्रशांत युद्ध|hr|Rat na Pacifiku|hy|Խաղաղօվկիանոսյան պատերազմ|id|Perang Pasifik|it|Guerra del Pacifico (1941-1945)|ja|太平洋戦争|jv|Perang Pasifik|ka|წყნარი ოკეანის კამპანიები|ko|태평양 전쟁|la|Bellum Pacificum|lb|Pazifikkrich|lfn|Gera de la Pasifica (1937-1945)|lt|Karas Ramiajame vandenyne|lv|Klusā okeāna karš|ml|പസഫിക് യുദ്ധം|ms|Perang Pasifik|ne|प्रशान्त युद्ध|nl|Azië in de Tweede Wereldoorlog|no|Stillehavskrigen|pl|Wojna na Pacyfiku|pnb|بحر الکاہل جنگ|ps|د ارام سمندر جګړه|pt|Guerra do Pacífico|ro|Războiul din Pacific (Al Doilea Război Mondial)|ru|Тихоокеанский театр военных действий Второй мировой войны|sh|Rat na Pacifiku|simple|Pacific War|sk|Vojna v Pacifiku|sl|Vojna za Tihi ocean|sq|Lufta e Paqësorit|sr|Рат на Пацифику|su|Perang Pasifik|sv|Stillahavskriget|ta|பசிபிக் போர்|th|สงครามแปซิฟิก|tl|Digmaang Pasipiko|tr|Pasifik Cephesi (II. Dünya Savaşı)|uk|Тихоокеанський театр воєнних дій Другої світової війни|ur|بحر الکاہل جنگ|uz|Tinch okeanidagi urush|vi|Chiến tranh Thái Bình Dương|wuu|太平洋战争|zh|太平洋战争|zh_min_nan|Thài-pêng-iûⁿ Chiàn-cheng|zh_yue|太平洋戰爭|qid=Q184425|lt=Pacific War}}. 
[[Image:Tenryū River December 28, 2005.JPG|thumb|Tenryū river, upper reaches]]

After the end of World War II, the [[:en:Supreme Commander of the Allied Powers|American occupation authorities]] ordered the dissolution of Nippon Hassoden, which was divided into regional power companies. Central Japan came under {{ill|Chubu Electric Power|en|Chubu Electric Power|qid=Q1091203|lt=Chubu Electric Power}}, which inherited the various dams and projects on the Tenryū River, all of which were located in Nagano Prefecture. For develop of the hydroelectric potential of the river in Shizuoka Prefecture, the government turned to the [[:en:Electric Power Development Company|Electric Power Development Company]]. The new company, in part through [[:en:foreign aid|foreign aid]] loans from the {{ill|United Nations|en|United Nations|qid=Q1065|lt=United Nations}}, and with the use of new dam technologies completed the huge {{ill|Sakuma Dam|en|Sakuma Dam|qid=Q1141896|lt=Sakuma Dam}} in the 1956, at the time the 10th largest in the world. Further dams were completed in the 1960s and 1970s until the Completion of the {{ill|Funagira Dam|en|Funagira Dam|qid=Q5508715|lt=Funagira Dam}} in 1976 brought development of the Tenryū River to a close.

===Environmental consequences===
These dams have altered the once abundant flow of the Tenryū River, and the lower reaches of the river near its mouth are almost dry.

This has had the unexpected effect of greatly increased erosion on the coastline of Shizuoka Prefecture, near Hamamatsu, especially around the {{ill|Nakatajima Sand Dunes|en|Nakatajima Sand Dunes|qid=Q1963977|lt=Nakatajima Sand Dunes}}. Meanwhile, at the same time, the vast amount of sand and silt trapped in various dams upstream have resulted in greatly lowered operational lives than originally projected. Methods to increase dredging in dams and to channel the silt and sand downstream to the ocean via a series of pipelines have been explored.

The [[:en:Tenryū Hamanako Railroad Tenryū Hamanako Line|Tenryū Hamanako Railroad Tenryū Hamanako Line]] runs along the lower reaches of the Tenryū River valley, whereas the {{ill|Iida Line|en|Iida Line|qid=Q771305|lt=Iida Line}} runs along the upper reaches of the river into upper Shizuoka and Nagano prefectures, with a stop at {{ill|Sakuma Station|en|Sakuma Station|qid=Q776591|lt=Sakuma Station}} near the namesake dam.
